solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Insult dry revolutionary to make trouble

parts.note: to dis someone is slang for insulting them

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns things round, so the word for dry is read backwards

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne

explanation.surface: Someone is goaded into causing a scene by a rebel's dry put-down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' reverses the champagne term, giving TURB; 'dry' is the wine sense, not humour.
explanation.definitionFit: To disturb is to cause unrest or upset, which is stirring up trouble.

clue.text: Lawyer on board could be girlfriend material?

indicators.note: on in a down clue means sitting above, so this piece comes first

parts.note: DA is a district attorney, an American lawyer
a board is a table, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A lawyer at the boardroom table might be good dating material.
explanation.definitionFit: Datable describes someone suitable to go out with romantically, a prospective partner.

clue.text: A US talent travelling around Brunei, say

indicators.note: travelling around means moving about, so these letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: An American performer tours Brunei.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunei is ruled by a sultan, so it is an example of a sultanate.

clue.text: Range of places men go when away from home

indicators.note: away from means taken out of, so these letters are removed

parts.note: urinals are men's toilets
IN means at home

explanation.surface: A list of where men like to go while away from home.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests travel, but it is a toilet joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The Urals are a mountain range dividing Europe from Asia.

clue.text: Lawyer, possibly one employed by a landlord

definitions.meaning: a barrister belongs to the Bar, so is a person of the Bar
a pub landlord employs bar staff

explanation.definitionFit: A barperson serves drinks; read as a member of the legal Bar, it could be counsel.

clue.text: One contriving to deceive Bow musician?

definitions.meaning: a cheat or swindler, someone who fiddles accounts
the question mark admits Bow is also a London district

explanation.surface: A con artist turns out to be a street musician from Bow in East London.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is capitalised to suggest the East London district, but it is the violinist's bow.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiddler plays the violin, and in slang also someone who cheats or swindles.

clue.text: Sweet female magistrate to ignore joint

indicators.note: to ignore means to leave out, so this letter is dropped

parts.note: a magistrate is a judge in a lower court
J is slang for a cannabis joint

explanation.surface: A woman magistrate overlooks a cannabis offence, with sweets in the background.
explanation.definitionFit: Fudge is a soft confection made from sugar, butter and milk.

clue.text: A pitcher drunk at end of day's extremely reasonable

indicators.note: at end of says the jumbled letters come after the abbreviation
drunk means unsteady and jumbled, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A jug drunk at day's end is very good value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges the eight letters to IRTCHEAP; 'at end of' sets them after D, and the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirt cheap means extraordinarily inexpensive, very reasonably priced.

clue.text: Acquire skill in Latin and bring home the bacon

parts.note: to bring home the bacon is to earn a living

explanation.surface: Someone becomes good at Latin and makes money from it.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn is to gain knowledge or mastery of something by study.

clue.text: Soldiers on open stretch of land pull back

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of British army soldiers
a tract is a wide area of land

explanation.surface: Troops on an exposed piece of ground withdraw.
explanation.definitionFit: Retract means draw in or withdraw, like a cat's claws.

clue.text: Some agendas Lutheran backs in foreign city

indicators.note: the hidden letters go backwards, as if they back up
only some of the letters of these words are used, so the answer lies hidden in them

explanation.surface: A Lutheran minister supports certain items on agendas in a city abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' hides ASLUT across agendAS LUTheran; 'backs' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulsa is a city in Oklahoma, foreign from the British setter's point of view.

clue.text: Criminal arrested kidnapping black singer

indicators.note: kidnapping means seizing and holding, so one piece is held inside the other
criminal means crooked, so these letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A crook is arrested for snatching a black singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' rearranges ARRESTED into REDREAST, and 'kidnapping' puts B inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The robin redbreast is a songbird, so a singer in crossword terms.

clue.text: One supports French eatery moving lunchtime forward

indicators.note: moving one letter means taking it out and putting it back elsewhere in the word
forward says the moved letter goes earlier in the word, nearer the front

parts.note: a brasserie is a French-style restaurant
one o'clock is lunchtime, and one is I in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A French restaurant brings its lunch service earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving ... forward' shifts I (one o'clock) earlier in BRASSERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bra is an undergarment whose job is supporting the bust, hence one that supports.

clue.text: Tory seen with half-cut gals in line dance

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, the Tory party

indicators.note: half-cut means cut in half, so only the first half of the word is kept

explanation.surface: A Conservative is seen with tipsy women joining a line dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' reads as drunk, but it halves GALS to GA.
explanation.definitionFit: The conga is a Cuban dance performed in a single long line of people.

clue.text: Old Bill operating with great precision

parts.note: EX means former, as in ex-wife
once a bill passes and comes into operation it is an act

explanation.surface: The police, the Old Bill, are working very accurately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Bill' is British slang for the police; here 'Old' and 'Bill' are split.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact means accurate in every detail, i.e. marked by great precision.

clue.text: Best prohibit distribution of articles for leader?

parts.note: top means best or highest
to ban is to prohibit

indicators.note: distribution means spreading out, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a and an are the indefinite articles

explanation.surface: A top figure wants to outlaw the circulation of certain newspaper pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' looks like newspaper pieces but is grammar's A and AN, rearranged by 'distribution of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Top banana is informal for the chief or most important person in a group.

clue.text: Government soldiers first to take account

parts.note: the state is the governing body of a country
soldiers are men, a standard crossword equivalence

indicators.note: first to here means the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Government troops are the first to give their account of events.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement is a written or spoken account, such as one given to police.

clue.text: Guiding device in car given to holy group

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car
PI is short for pious, meaning holy
a lot is a group or set of things

explanation.surface: A car is handed over to a religious body.
explanation.definitionFit: An autopilot is a system that steers a plane or ship without a human.

clue.text: Passionate proposal to open fresh ale

indicators.note: to open means to split another piece apart and sit inside it
fresh means new, so the letters are made anew in a different order

parts.note: a motion is a formal proposal put to a meeting

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic suggestion to crack open some new beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' gives EAL, which 'to open' splits after the E to take the formal proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotional describes someone moved by strong feelings, ardent or fervent.

clue.text: Decide tomorrow what one might do with mattress?

definitions.meaning: to delay a decision until the next day

definitions.text: what one might do with mattress?
definitions.meaning: literally, one sleeps on a mattress

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means postponing a choice overnight; the literal sense is lying on the bed.

clue.text: Tolerate services being held up by a church

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means lifted so the letters read upwards

parts.note: MOTs are the annual roadworthiness tests that British cars undergo at a garage

explanation.surface: Church services are being delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'services' suggests worship, but means MOTs, the British vehicle checks; 'being held up' reverses them to STOM.
explanation.definitionFit: To stomach something is to put up with it or endure it.

clue.text: Idiot stealing head of state's cheap wine

indicators.note: stealing means taking something away, so these letters are removed

parts.note: plonker is British slang for a fool
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the Queen, the UK head of state

explanation.surface: A fool pinches the president's cheap bottle of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stealing' looks like taking something in, but here ER is taken away from PLONKER.
explanation.definitionFit: Plonk is British slang for inferior, inexpensive wine.

clue.text: Sort to get wine for family members

parts.note: a sort is a kind or type
red is red wine

explanation.surface: A type of person gets wine for the relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred means one's relatives, the people related by blood.

clue.text: Old Frenchman I finally understand in city abroad

parts.note: M is short for Monsieur, a Frenchman's title
aha is what one says when at last understanding something

explanation.surface: An elderly Frenchman says he has at last understood something in a city overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' looks like a last-letter signal, but the whole phrase is spoken as AHA.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is a city in Nebraska, abroad from the British setter's perspective.

clue.text: Parrot scooping up small piece of nut tree

indicators.note: scooping up means gathering into itself, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to parrot is to ape, copy someone

indicators.note: a piece of here means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A parrot picks up a little bit of nut from a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parrot' is the verb to copy, giving APE.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen is a poplar known for its trembling leaves.

clue.text: Prunes cooked with oil could create this

definitions.text: Prunes cooked with oil could create this

indicators.note: cooked means messed with or prepared, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A dish of prunes cooked in oil would turn anyone's stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: 'cooked' rearranges PRUNES plus OIL, and the dish described would cause disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: Repulsion is strong disgust, which such an unappetising dish might provoke.

clue.text: In high spirits, removing top is perilous

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is taken off

parts.note: frisky means playful and lively

explanation.surface: A cheerful person stripping off a top is taking a chance.
explanation.definitionFit: Risky means involving danger or the chance of harm.

clue.text: Legless leader on port must be loaded

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the preceding word

parts.note: Aden is a port city in Yemen

explanation.surface: A drunk ship's captain in harbour must be full of cargo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legless' is British slang for very drunk; here only its leading L is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means weighed down with a load, so carrying cargo.

clue.text: Evaluation of artist one's found in shock

indicators.note: found in means sitting inside, so these pieces go within the other

parts.note: to appal is to shock or horrify
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
one is I, and one's is I'S, i.e. I plus S

explanation.surface: A critic's review of a painter turns up in a state of shock.
explanation.definitionFit: An appraisal is an assessment of something's worth or quality.

clue.text: One spotted around new river restaurant

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a die is one of a pair of dice, marked with spots

explanation.surface: Someone is seen near a fresh riverside restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted' suggests being seen, but it describes a die with its spots.
explanation.definitionFit: A diner is an inexpensive American-style eatery serving simple meals.

clue.text: Country suspended head of ailing railway

parts.note: hung means suspended or hanging

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: The rail service is halted because its sick boss has been suspended.
explanation.definitionFit: Hungary is a landlocked nation in Central Europe.

clue.text: Foremost of trawlermen fished with lines crossed?

indicators.note: foremost of means the leading letter of the following word

parts.note: angled means fished with a rod and line

explanation.surface: The leading trawlerman fished until his lines got snarled up.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangled means twisted and knotted together, as fishing lines get when crossed.
